sections.overview: The Desert grizzled skipper is a small butterfly of North Africa, eastern Africa, Arabia and parts of western and southern Asia.
sections.identification: It is a skipper in the family Hesperiidae; taxonomic accounts recognize several geographically separated forms within the species.
sections.habitat: It uses desert and semi-desert plains, foothills and rocky dry habitats.
sections.diet: Larvae feed on bindweeds, including Convolvulus species; adults visit flowers for nectar.
sections.behavior: Field accounts report adults visiting flowers; an Indian record describes one resting on a grass inflorescence in arid, rocky habitat.
sections.reproduction: Flight periods vary by locality, and published accounts describe more than one seasonal flight in some regions; early stages remain poorly documented.
sections.ecology: The Indian form evanida was rediscovered in the Thar Desert after a long gap in records, illustrating how little some regional populations are observed.
sections.conservation: The Mediterranean IUCN assessment lists the species as Least Concern in that region; this is not a global category.
